faqs.question: How should epoxy coatings be applied in Oman's hot climate?
faqs.answer: Epoxy coating application in Oman's hot climate requires careful temperature management because high temperatures dramatically accelerate pot life and cure speed. Standard two-component epoxy coatings have a pot life of 30–60 minutes at 23°C; at Oman's summer ambient temperatures of 38–50°C, pot life can shorten to 10–20 minutes, making large-volume mixing impractical. Best practices for Oman: mix only small batches (2–5 kg) to complete within pot life; begin work in the early morning (5:00–9:00 AM) when surface temperatures are lowest; avoid application when the steel surface temperature exceeds 50°C (measure with surface thermometer); ensure the surface temperature is at least 3°C above the dew point to prevent moisture condensation on freshly applied coating; and use a heat-stabilised epoxy formulation where summer application is unavoidable. Film thickness must be verified wet (wet film gauge) and dry (Elcometer DFT meter) to confirm the specified DFT is achieved. Relative humidity above 85% affects epoxy cure — although less common in Oman's interior, coastal areas during the Khareef monsoon period in Salalah can reach high humidity. Global Chemicals LLC provides application support for all supplied epoxy systems.

title: Epoxy Resin & Hardener
description: Two-component epoxy resin system for floors, grouting, bonding, repair mortars and laminating.

details.longDescription: Epoxy resin supplier in Oman - Global Chemicals LLC supplies two-component epoxy resin systems — a liquid bisphenol-A epoxy resin and a matched hardener — for construction, flooring and industrial maintenance in Muscat, Sohar, Duqm, Salalah and across the GCC. The resin and hardener are mixed in the ratio stated on the technical data sheet and cure by chemical reaction into a hard, chemically resistant solid, so the same chemistry can be supplied for several jobs: self-levelling and screed floors, epoxy grout for machine bases and anchor bolts, bonding new concrete to old, epoxy repair mortars (mixed with graded sand or filler), crack injection (with a low-viscosity injection grade), and glass-fibre laminating and tank lining. The hardener decides how the system behaves: polyamide hardeners give longer working time and good adhesion on damp concrete, cycloaliphatic and modified amine hardeners give faster cure and better chemical resistance, and phenalkamine hardeners cure at low temperature or in humid conditions. In Oman's summer heat the reaction runs faster, so mix small batches, work in the cooler hours and store the components out of direct sun. Both components can cause skin sensitisation: wear nitrile gloves and eye protection, and do not leave mixed material in a large mass, which heats up as it cures. Each supply comes with a technical data sheet and safety data sheets for both components; delivery covers Oman by road, with export to the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain.

faqs.question: What is the difference between epoxy resin and an epoxy coating?
faqs.answer: An epoxy coating is a finished, ready-to-apply formulation (resin, hardener, pigments and additives) designed to be rolled or sprayed as a protective film. Epoxy resin and hardener are the base binder: the same chemistry, supplied so that you can make grout, repair mortar, self-levelling floor or laminate by adding graded sand, fillers or glass fibre as your method statement requires. Global Chemicals LLC supplies both; for a finished floor or tank lining choose the epoxy coating, and for grouting, bonding, mortar or laminating choose the resin and hardener.

faqs.question: Which epoxy hardener should I choose?
faqs.answer: Choose by working conditions and the performance you need. Polyamide hardeners give a longer working time, flexibility and good adhesion to damp concrete, which suits general bonding and primers. Modified and cycloaliphatic amine hardeners cure faster and give better chemical resistance and a harder surface, which suits industrial floors and chemical bunds. Phenalkamine hardeners keep curing at low temperature and in high humidity. In Oman and the GCC the main issue is heat: every system cures faster above 30°C, so mix only what can be applied within the pot life. Tell us the application, the substrate and the site temperature, and we will recommend the resin and hardener combination with its data sheet.

title: Construction Sealants
description: Silicone, polyurethane and acrylic sealants for movement joints, glazing, facades and sanitary areas.

details.longDescription: Construction sealant supplier in Oman - Global Chemicals LLC supplies silicone, polyurethane (PU) and acrylic sealants for contractors, facade installers and maintenance teams in Muscat, Sohar, Duqm, Salalah and across the GCC. The three families do different jobs. Neutral-cure silicone sealants stay elastic over a wide temperature range and resist UV, so they are used for weather sealing of glazing, curtain walls and window perimeters (structural glazing needs a structural silicone approved by the glazing system supplier); acetoxy (vinegar-smell) silicones are for sanitary and glass work and should not be used on metals, stone or concrete that the released acid can stain or corrode. Polyurethane sealants bond strongly to concrete and can be painted over, so they are the usual choice for expansion and control joints in floors, pavements, car parks and precast panels. Acrylic sealants are paintable, water-based and easy to tool, and suit interior gaps around frames and plasterboard where joint movement is small. For any moving joint the sealant must be applied over a backer rod so it bonds to the two sides only, at the depth the data sheet specifies, and the joint faces must be clean, dry and primed where required. In Oman's heat and sun, choose a UV-stable silicone or PU for exposed joints. Each supply comes with technical and safety data sheets; delivery covers Oman by road, with export to the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain.

faqs.question: Silicone, polyurethane or acrylic sealant: which should I use?
faqs.answer: Use neutral-cure silicone for weather sealing glazing, curtain walls, windows and any joint exposed to strong sun (structural glazing needs a structural silicone approved by the glazing system supplier), because it stays elastic and UV-stable over a wide temperature range; it cannot be painted. Use polyurethane for expansion and control joints in concrete floors, pavements, car parks and precast panels, where you need strong adhesion to concrete, abrasion resistance and a paintable finish. Use acrylic for interior, low-movement gaps that will be painted. Acetoxy silicone is only for sanitary and glass work, never on metals, stone or concrete. If the joint is a designed movement joint, choose a sealant whose movement class (ISO 11600 / ASTM C920) matches the movement on the drawings.

faqs.question: How do I size a sealant joint and the backer rod?
faqs.answer: For most elastic sealants the joint should be about twice as wide as the sealant is deep, with a minimum width and depth of 6 mm (for joints narrower than about 12 mm the depth equals the width), and the joint width must allow for the expected movement divided by the sealant's movement capability. Insert a closed-cell backer rod about 25% wider than the joint so it sits firmly and sets the sealant depth, and stops the sealant bonding to the joint base (three-sided adhesion makes joints tear). Clean and dry the joint faces, apply primer where the data sheet requires it, gun the sealant in, and tool it to a slightly concave finish. Always follow the depth and width limits on the product data sheet.

title: Paraffin Oil
description: Industrial grade paraffin oil for construction applications and formulations.

details.longDescription:
Paraffin oil (liquid paraffin, light mineral oil, CAS 8012-95-1) is a refined petroleum oil. It is supplied here as an industrial grade for construction: a clear, colourless oil of 10–30 cSt at 40 °C, specific gravity 0.82–0.88 and flash point 150 °C minimum, in 200 L drums and bulk, for precast factories, ready-mix and site contractors, formwork suppliers and makers of release agents.

Its main construction use is as form release (shutter) oil. A thin, even film on steel, timber or plywood formwork and on precast moulds stops concrete bonding to the face, so forms strip cleanly and can be reused. It is used neat, or as the base and carrier oil in formulated release agents, which add surfactants or fatty-acid components that react with the cement. Applied too heavily it can leave stains, surface dusting and blowholes, so it is sprayed or wiped to the thinnest continuous film; and it is applied before reinforcement is fixed, or kept off the steel, because oil on rebar weakens the bond. Oiling timber and plywood forms also reduces their water uptake, and contractors coat tools, chutes and plant with it to stop concrete build-up.

Light mineral oils are also sprayed on some aggregates and unpaved surfaces to keep dust down, and serve as a base oil for lubricants. Paraffin oil is not a curing compound on its own: the membranes that hold water in fresh concrete are wax, resin or acrylic formulations, and mineral oil is at most a carrier in some of them. Viscosity is the main choice: lower-viscosity oil sprays more easily and spreads thinner, higher-viscosity oil clings better to vertical faces. Solid paraffin wax is listed separately on this site.

Handling and storage: low-viscosity mineral oils are classified H304, may be fatal if swallowed and enters airways; the classification applies to oils of 20.5 cSt or less at 40 °C, so the lower end of this range carries it. If swallowed, do not induce vomiting; get medical help. It is not regulated for transport. Avoid breathing spray mist by using the coarsest spray that gives an even film and working with ventilation, and wear oil-resistant gloves and goggles, as repeated contact dries and irritates the skin. Spills make decks and floors slippery. It is combustible, though not easily ignited: keep it away from strong oxidisers and ignition sources, store drums closed, under cover and out of direct sun, and do not let oil or washings reach drains or soil.

It is supplied in 200 L drums and in bulk, with a safety data sheet. Ask for the certificate of analysis and for the viscosity that suits your spray equipment and formwork with your quote.

faqs.question: What is a polymer bonding agent and when is it used in Oman construction?
faqs.answer: A polymer bonding agent (typically SBR — styrene-butadiene rubber latex, or acrylic polymer) is a liquid chemical additive applied to existing concrete or masonry surfaces before applying new render, screed, or repair mortar to promote adhesion between the old and new substrates. Without a bonding agent, new cement-based material applied to dense, smooth, or contaminated old concrete tends to debond (delaminate) within months as differential movement and thermal cycling cause interface failure. In Oman's hot climate, where daily temperature swings of 15–25°C create significant thermal expansion and contraction in concrete structures, bonding agent application is standard practice for all concrete repair and overlay work. Application method: the bonding agent (diluted SBR latex 1:1 with water for most applications) is brushed onto the prepared substrate and allowed to become 'tacky' (not dry) before applying the fresh concrete overlay. The polymer chains from the bonding agent penetrate both surfaces and form a physical and chemical bond across the interface. Global Chemicals LLC supplies SBR and acrylic polymer bonding agents for Oman's construction repair and maintenance sector.
